lines.en: Hey, Ana! **How was your weekend?** Did you do anything fun?
lines.pt: Oi, Ana! Como foi o seu fim de semana? Você fez algo divertido?

lines.en: **It was** great! **I visited** my cousin in Chicago on Saturday.
lines.pt: Foi ótimo! Visitei minha prima em Chicago no sábado.

lines.en: No, **I didn’t.** We drove, because the train tickets were expensive.
lines.pt: Não. Fomos de carro, porque as passagens de trem estavam caras.

lines.en: Makes sense. What did you do there?
lines.pt: Faz sentido. O que vocês fizeram lá?

lines.en: **We didn’t** have much time, so we just walked by the lake and ate pizza.
lines.pt: Não tivemos muito tempo, então só caminhamos perto do lago e comemos pizza.

lines.en: I stayed home and cleaned. It was boring! **How about you?**
lines.pt: Fiquei em casa e limpei. Foi chato! E você?

lines.en: I played soccer here in the park, then I watched a movie. We lost, but it was fun!
lines.pt: Joguei futebol aqui no parque e depois assisti a um filme. Perdemos, mas foi divertido!

pages.title: Telling Someone About Your Weekend

situation.text: It is Monday morning. You meet a friend in the park and they ask about your weekend. You tell a short story, answer follow-up questions and ask about theirs.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can tell a short story about your weekend, answer questions about what you did and ask a friend about theirs — in the past, naturally.
canDo: Say what you did: I visited… / I stayed…
Answer Yes/No questions: Did you…? — Yes, I did. / No, I didn’t.
Say what did not happen: We didn’t…
Give an opinion about the event: It was great / boring.
success: I say one thing that did not happen.
pages.think: When a friend asks about your weekend in Portuguese, do you answer with one word or tell a little story? And in English?

teach.goal: Abrir a aula pela situação real, não pela regra.
solo: Leia o objetivo e peça que o estudante diga, com as próprias palavras, o que vai conseguir fazer hoje.
Faça a pergunta “Think about it” antes de mostrar qualquer expressão.
group: Cada estudante diz uma palavra ou ideia que associa à situação.
Mostre os critérios de sucesso: eles são a missão final da aula.
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about the student’s life, not a grammar test.
intro.group: One question per student, then a follow-up question to a classmate.

pages.recall: Daily routines: “I usually…”. Ask: What do you usually do on Saturdays?

qs.q: How’s your week going so far?
qs.pt: Como está a sua semana até agora?

qs.q: What did you eat for lunch yesterday?
Did you watch anything good this month?
qs.pt: Você assistiu algo bom neste mês?

pages.tip: Use the answers to find gaps and to recycle earlier content. The goal is to enter English from the first minute.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma no primeiro minuto e mapear lacunas.
extra: What did you do last night?
support: Ofereça as respostas-modelo (chips) e peça apenas que escolham uma e a ampliem com um motivo.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Monday small talk
pages.intro: In the USA, “How was your weekend?” is the classic Monday question. People expect a short story, not just “good”. Look and guess before you read.

cards.pt: Como foi o seu fim de semana?
cards.note: A very common Monday question at work and at school.
“Good! I visited my cousin — we walked by the lake.”
Returning the question keeps the conversation going.

qs.q: What do people usually say after “How was your weekend?”
qs.pt: O que as pessoas costumam responder?

levels.A2: They say it was good and tell one thing they did.
levels.B1: They give a short answer, one detail, and ask the same question back.
levels.B2: A good answer has an evaluation, one concrete detail and a return question, which makes small talk feel warm.

qs.pt: Por que “How about you?” é importante?

levels.A2: It shows I am interested in you.
levels.B1: It turns a monologue into a conversation and shows interest.
levels.B2: Returning the question is a social signal: it shares the turn and keeps the interaction balanced.

qs.q: How long should a weekend story be?
qs.pt: Quão longa deve ser a história?

levels.A2: Two or three sentences are enough.
levels.B1: Two or three sentences with one detail; you can say more if the other person asks.
levels.B2: Keep it brief and offer a hook; let the listener decide whether to ask for more.

pages.compare: In Brazil you might answer “Foi tranquilo” and the talk moves on. In the USA people usually add a detail and ask back. Which feels more natural to you?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural e as primeiras hipóteses.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que compare com o que acontece no Brasil.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.
answers: Q1: avaliação + detalhe + pergunta de volta.
Q2: mostra interesse e divide o turno de fala.
extra: Do you ask about the weekend at work?
What detail do you like to share?
support: Use as respostas de nível A1 como andaime e peça que repitam.
stretch: B2: compare o registro e o tom entre Brasil e EUA com exemplos reais.

pass1.q: What are the friends talking about?
pass1.pt: Sobre o que os amigos conversam?

tasks.label: What did Ana do on Sunday?

teach.goal: Compreender a situação antes de ver o texto: ideia principal e depois informações específicas.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: só a ideia principal.
2ª escuta: peça os detalhes pedidos nas tarefas. Só depois mostre o texto.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam antes de revelar.
Compare as respostas entre duplas e só então mostre o texto.
answers: Pass 2: Chicago · drove · pizza · soccer · cleaned
extra: How does Ana feel about Saturday? And Sunday?
Who has the better weekend, in your opinion?
support: Pause depois de cada fala se necessário.

qs.q: What did Ana do on Sunday?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê um papel e você lê o outro; depois troquem.
Peça que reconte a conversa no nível que conseguir.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante.
answers: Her cousin · The train tickets were expensive · She cleaned at home · They lost
extra: What would YOU say about last weekend?
What follow-up question would you ask Ana?
support: Mostre a tradução (botão PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.pt: Como foi o seu fim de semana?
items.alt: Also: **Did you have a good weekend?**

items.use: Give a quick opinion about the event.
Say what you did without making it a big deal.

pages.note: Instead of memorizing the whole list, choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again. The others are for understanding and for stretching later.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks para uso repetido e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de dar o significado.
Compare formal × informal e peça um exemplo próprio.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão que mais usaria e explica quando.
Comparem equivalentes em duplas.
answers: Starting small talk · Telling what you did · Asking about the past · Saying what did not happen · Reacting
extra: Which expression do you use most with friends?
How can you say It was great! in another way?

errors.r: It was a lot of fun. / It was really fun.

support: Trabalhe só as expressões ★ nesta aula.

patterns.name: Questions and short answers
ex: Yes, I did. / No, I didn’t.

patterns.name: Negatives
ex: I didn’t go out on Sunday.

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: We spent the afternoon walking around the lake.
We did not do very much.
register.note: Contractions like didn’t are normal in speech; in formal writing people often write did not.

teach.goal: Fixar os padrões principais (01 e 02); os outros são expansão. Usar a troca de palavras para variar a fala.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo (grife os chunks).
Use “Swap the words”: toque em cada peça e peça que o estudante diga a frase completa.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça e o próximo repete a frase.
Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Padrões 01 e 02 são o foco; 03 e 04 são expansão para quem avançar rápido.
extra: Change one word and say the sentence again.
Say one true and one false sentence; your partner guesses.
support: Fique só com o padrão 01 na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combine dois padrões na mesma resposta.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Regular past verbs end in three sounds: /t/ (walked), /d/ (cleaned) and /ɪd/ (visited). You do not say a full “ed” every time.

own.prompt: Write a true sentence about last weekend with a regular verb (walked, cleaned, visited…).
own.criteria: Say it twice. Did walked end with a quick /t/ and visited with an extra syllable?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno de pronúncia: The -ed ending.
solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar, reproduzir ritmo e entonação, usar em frase com conteúdo próprio.
Modele devagar e em velocidade normal; peça que bata palmas na sílaba forte.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante cria uma frase própria usando o fenômeno.
answers: Identify: We walked by the lake. · I visited my cousin.
extra: Which -ed sound is hardest for you?
support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas em voz alta.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. A friend asks: “How was your weekend?”
opts: It was great! I visited my aunt.
items.why: Give an evaluation + one detail in the past.

items.q: 2. “Did you go to the beach?” You did not go.

items.why: After didn’t, use the base verb: have.

items.q: 4. Your friend says: “I stayed home and cleaned.” Best reaction?
opts: Oh, that sounds relaxing. How about the evening?
items.why: React, then ask a natural follow-up question.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

items.text: ___ you watch the game on Sunday?
items.why: Did + subject + base verb for questions.

opts: I stayed home and read a book.
items.why: Answer with a past action and one detail.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado: escolher, completar, substituir e responder antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que o estudante justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça uma versão mais informal ou mais educada.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: It was great! I visited my aunt. · No, I didn’t. · We didn’t have time. · Oh, that sounds relaxing. How about the evening? · ate · Did · I didn’t play soccer. · Did you visit your cousin? · I stayed home and read a book.
extra: Say each correct answer aloud with natural rhythm.
support: Ofereça o banco de palavras (chips) nas lacunas.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — tell your weekend story

brief.teacher: You are a friend on Monday morning. Ask about the weekend and add a surprising follow-up question.
brief.student: You are the friend: tell what you really did, answer the questions and ask back.

orders: A weekend trip to see family
A weekend with a party or a game
complications: Your friend asks about something you didn’t do.
You forgot the word for what you did: explain it another way.
Your friend says they did the same thing: react and compare.
Your friend didn’t hear you: repeat and clarify.
success: I say one thing that did not happen.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação inesperada e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Combine o cenário com a vida real do estudante.
Rodada 1: com chunks. Rodada 2: só palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Meta de fala: 60–70% do tempo para o estudante. Anote 2–3 correções para a devolutiva.
extra: What if the friend asks for more details? What do you add?
support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça que repita só a primeira frase.
stretch: Acrescente uma segunda complicação no meio da cena.

rounds.title: Tell it
rounds.task: Tell your partner two things you did last weekend.

rounds.title: Ask more
rounds.task: Ask two Did you…? questions about your partner’s weekend.

rounds.title: Not this time
rounds.task: Say two things you didn’t do and why.

rounds.title: Retell
rounds.task: Whole group: retell your partner’s weekend in three sentences.

infogap.title: Whose weekend?
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: Dan’s weekend (you know Saturday)
a.task: You know Saturday. Ask what Dan did on Sunday and how it was.

b.title: Dan’s weekend (you know Sunday)
b.task: You know Sunday. Ask what Dan did on Saturday and how it was.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição da função com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada (A+B / C+D → A+C / B+D → A+D / B+C → grupo todo).
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
Circule anotando 2–3 correções prioritárias.
answers: A sabe sábado (visited a museum · great); B sabe domingo (cooked with friends · delicious). Cada um pergunta “What did Dan do on…?” e “How was it?”.
support: Entregue frases-modelo no chat da turma.

pages.title: Group mission — the Monday catch-up
pages.goal: Each group must hold a real Monday conversation: tell a story, ask follow-up questions and say what did not happen.

missions.mission: One friend visited family far away; the other asks how the trip was and why they chose that transport.
missions.constraint: Use “Did you…?” twice and “I didn’t…” once.

missions.mission: One friend had a boring weekend at home; the other tries to find one good thing about it.
missions.constraint: Use “It was…” and ask “How about you?”
missions.start: Hi! Did you do anything fun?

missions.mission: Both friends did a sport or an event; compare what happened and who won or lost.
missions.constraint: Use three regular past verbs with -ed.
missions.start: So, what did you do on Saturday?

success: I say one thing that did not happen.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: o objetivo é resolver, não só falar certo.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão. Alterne os papéis.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com frases de apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Observe e anote 2–3 correções prioritárias; devolutiva no fim.
answers: Modelo: “How was your weekend?” → “It was great! I visited my cousin.” → “Did you take the train?” → “No, I didn’t. We drove.”
support: Dê o início de frase (“Start with”) em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a friend about your weekend. Say two things you did, one thing you didn’t do and how it was.
pages.model: Hi Tom! **How was your weekend?** Mine was great. **I visited my cousin** and we walked by the lake. **We didn’t** go to the museum because it was closed. **It was** a really nice day. How about you?
checklist: I used at least two past verbs.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos e corrijam em duplas.

errors.w: I stay at home on Sunday.
errors.r: I stayed at home on Sunday.

support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You told your story with past verbs and a clear detail.
prompts.improve: Example: Use did + base verb in questions (Did you go…?, not Did you went…?).
prompts.next: Example: Tell a story with a beginning, a problem and an end.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

tasks.name: Build a question
tasks.prompt: Without notes: ask if your friend took the train.

tasks.name: Respond to a situation
tasks.prompt: A friend asks: “How was your weekend?” You stayed home.
tasks.model: It was quiet. I stayed home and cleaned.

tasks.name: Use a new expression
tasks.prompt: Say you did not have time.

items: Record a 45–60 second audio telling your weekend.
Write three sentences: two things you did and one thing you didn’t.
Learn five irregular past verbs (went, ate, saw, had, drove) and use them.
Listen to the dialogue again and notice every -ed sound.

unit: Tell · describe · compare · book · opine · advise · plan

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem consultar as anotações: construir uma pergunta, responder a uma situação e usar uma expressão nova.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega e combine a tarefa de continuidade.
answers: Did you take the train? · It was quiet. I stayed home and cleaned. · We didn’t have much time.
extra: Revisão espaçada: retomar o passado simples na próxima aula e na missão final da unidade.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Say one simple thing. Short phrases and models.

ladder.say: I visited my cousin, but we didn’t have much time.
ladder.goal: Tell a short past story with details.

ladder.say: We were supposed to go out, but it rained, so we stayed in and watched a series.
It was one of those weekends where nothing went as planned, yet it turned out to be oddly relaxing.
We ended up improvising the whole trip, which, in hindsight, made it more memorable.
It was the sort of weekend that slips by quietly and leaves you, oddly, more rested than a holiday would.
ladder.goal: Tell it with style and implication.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
extra: Which sentence would you like to be able to say next month?
